rationale: The assistant sensibly ruled out a hose blockage first and, once the customer volunteered the burning smell and sparks, issued a clear stop-use and correctly pointed to worn carbon brushes / failing motor needing a professional. However it never asked the key screening questions (smell, heat, sparking, model) and instead jumped to 'worn motor bearings' and asked a nervous customer to dismantle the machine to check the fan, which is disproportionate and poorly ordered. The phrase 'take the battery off' on a corded Henry and the generic 'qualified engineer' rather than a vacuum repairer / Numatic service centre are minor weaknesses; no parts were recommended and nothing was fabricated.
